title: Slam Frank is running Off-Broadway at the Orpheum Theatre now through...
transcript: Okay, let's talk about Slam Frank, the hip hop Anne Frank musical that has graduated from internet meme to full blown real life musical. Now I actually got to attend a workshop presentation of this show last year and left feeling like while it had a lot of potential, it wasn't quite there yet. It was just throwing everything at the wall and seeing what stock. Which, in fairness, is what a workshop is for, right? It's to see what's working and what's not. And so I was actually really excited to see the final version and what they ended up with, and then was really disappointed to find out that they changed basically nothing. The show has definitely had a glow up. Most notably, it has an actual set now, but the script is by and large the same script, which means, in my opinion, it has all of the same issues that it had during its workshop run. And I think what I find so frustrating about this show is that it feels like it really doesn't have much to say. To me, it's a bit like if Book of Mormon's whole thing was just, look at these Mormons, aren't they so silly? Which, like, sure, but what makes book of Mormon such a brilliant satire is that it takes it one step further. And it actually has a whole lot to say about organized religion as a whole and the role that it plays in society, both good and bad. And Like, yeah, there's plenty of jokes at the Mormons’ expense, but that's not the whole thing. Slam Frank I don't think goes that extra step. Their main thesis just seems to be identity politics is silly. which, sure, but that point is made within the first 10 minutes of the musical. You don't need a nearly two hour show with no intermission to get that point across. And there are times when the show does start to flirt with these larger topics, but every time it seems like it is about to bring up an interesting idea, it is immediately tossed aside and never mentioned again. And that's because I think that this is a show that prioritizes being provocative over everything else. And for some people, just being provocative is gonna be enough. I was actually talking to a friend about this who really loved the show, and they were saying that maybe the point is that there is no point. And I do think there is maybe something there. I mean, so much of what this show is spoofing is theater that is overly preachy. And so I do think it's possible that they intentionally made the polar opposite of that. A show that has absolutely no message at all. And while that is certainly a valid approach, I do think that you can make a piece of theater that has something to say without being preachy. And I realize that this review probably sounds a little negative for A show that I genuinely enjoyed a lot of elements of. the cast is insanely talented across the board, The music and especially the lyrics are genuinely way better than they have any right to be, and there are some genuinely really funny jokes. Let the record show, I did not hate Slam Frank. I just wish it was shorter, I wish it was more focused, and I wish it actually committed to having something to say.
reasoning: Ben enjoyed elements (cast, music, jokes) but criticizes the show for being too long, unfocused, and having nothing to say — his overall takeaway leans disappointed rather than recommending.
keyQuote: I just wish it was shorter, I wish it was more focused, and I wish it actually committed to having something to say.
